validated_results.title: Fatty foods and the risk of bladder cancer: A case-control study.
validated_results.reason: Case-control study reporting an adjusted odds ratio for milk and dairy product intake and newly diagnosed bladder cancer.

extraction.timing: retrospective dietary assessment (food intake within 1 y)
extraction.population: Patients newly diagnosed with bladder cancer and recruited controls

sample_size.excerpt: Patients newly diagnosed with bladder cancer (n = 113) and 292 controls were recruited.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 113 + 292 = 405

cases.excerpt: Patients newly diagnosed with bladder cancer (n = 113) and 292 controls were recruited.

effect_size.excerpt: After adjusting for potential confounders, the intakes of marine fish and milk and dairy products were negatively correlated with bladder cancer, with the adjusted OR of 0.28 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.55) and 0.36 (95% CI, 0.19-0.69). Total nuts were related to a 76% reduction in bladder cancer risk (OR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12-0.48).

confidence_interval.excerpt: After adjusting for potential confounders, the intakes of marine fish and milk and dairy products were negatively correlated with bladder cancer, with the adjusted OR of 0.28 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.55) and 0.36 (95% CI, 0.19-0.69).
